concepts.preferred_label: Chronic Graft-Versus-Host Disease of the Eye
concepts.why: The patient's chronic eye symptoms, subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, corneal neovascularizations, and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with chronic graft-versus-host disease of the eye.
The patient's subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, corneal neovascularizations, and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with ocular cicatricial pemphigoid.
The patient's corneal neovascularizations and reduction in conjunctival hyperemia and corneal vascularizations after treatment are consistent with corneal lymphangiectasia.
The patient's subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with conjunctival scarring.
The patient's chronic eye symptoms and vision deterioration are consistent with dry eye syndrome.
The patient's corneal neovascularizations and reduction in conjunctival hyperemia and corneal vascularizations after treatment are consistent with corneal ulcer.
The patient's chronic eye symptoms, subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with Sjögren's syndrome.
The patient's subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, corneal neovascularizations, and conjunctival hyperemia are consistent with Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
